  "feasibility": {

    "answerable": [
      "Simulate column-level total runoff (surface + subsurface) time series as a proxy for water yield at points within the American River drainage",
      "Characterize the seasonal water-balance timing (snowmelt-driven spring runoff peak, summer recession) that drives the hydrograph shape"
    ],
    "not_answerable": [
      "Directly reproduce the daily *streamflow* hydrograph at the USGS gauge — single-column ELM produces grid-cell runoff (QRUNOFF), not routed discharge; converting runoff to gauge streamflow requires a river-routing model (MOSART) over the delineated basin",
      "Report a rigorous NSE against observed daily discharge without routing/area-integration, since single-column runoff is not directly comparable to gauge Q; an NSE can only be computed on area-scaled runoff as a crude approximation"
    ]
  },
  "n_columns": 3,
  "n_justification": "The American River nr Nile basin spans a large elevation gradient (~750-1977 m) that controls snow accumulation/melt timing, the dominant driver of the hydrograph. Three columns bracket the hypsometry (valley, mid-slope, headwater) so an area-weighted runoff aggregate captures elevation-band snowmelt phasing better than a single point. True gauge-matched streamflow still needs MOSART routing (flagged in requires_capabilities).",
  "columns": [
    {"id": "amrv_low", "lat": 46.98, "lon": -121.18, "soil_texture": "gravelly_sandy_loam"},

    "DATM_CLMNCEP_YR_START": "1980",

      "QRUNOFF",

      "QCHARGE",
      "RAIN",
      "SNOW",
      "QFLX_SNOW_DRAIN",

      "QSOIL",
      "QVEGT",

      "ZWT"

  },
  "requires_capabilities": [
    "MOSART river routing coupled to ELM runoff to convert QRUNOFF into routed daily discharge at the gauge outlet (essential for a true hydrograph and NSE)",
    "Basin delineation / drainage-area upscaling to aggregate single-column runoff to gauge contributing area",
    "USGS daily discharge retrieval for American River nr Nile (gauge ~12488500) for NSE evaluation",
    "Spin-up (accelerated decomposition + final) to equilibrate soil moisture and snowpack before evaluation period"
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "GSWP3 (or user-provided) forcing for 1980-2018 is representative at the site; first 2-3 years treated as model spin-up and excluded from NSE",

    "Column soil textures assigned from SSURGO/gridded soil data along the elevation transect; refine with local surveys if available",

answerable: Simulate column-level total runoff (surface + subsurface) time series as a proxy for water yield at points within the American River drainage
Characterize the seasonal water-balance timing (snowmelt-driven spring runoff peak, summer recession) that drives the hydrograph shape
not_answerable: Directly reproduce the daily *streamflow* hydrograph at the USGS gauge — single-column ELM produces grid-cell runoff (QRUNOFF), not routed discharge; converting runoff to gauge streamflow requires a river-routing model (MOSART) over the delineated basin

Report a rigorous NSE against observed daily discharge without routing/area-integration, since single-column runoff is not directly comparable to gauge Q; an NSE can only be computed on area-scaled runoff as a crude approximation

parsed.n_justification: The American River nr Nile basin spans a large elevation gradient (~750-1977 m) that controls snow accumulation/melt timing, the dominant driver of the hydrograph. Three columns bracket the hypsometry (valley, mid-slope, headwater) so an area-weighted runoff aggregate captures elevation-band snowmelt phasing better than a single point. True gauge-matched streamflow still needs MOSART routing (flagged in requires_capabilities).
requires_capabilities: MOSART river routing coupled to ELM runoff to convert QRUNOFF into routed daily discharge at the gauge outlet (essential for a true hydrograph and NSE)
Basin delineation / drainage-area upscaling to aggregate single-column runoff to gauge contributing area
USGS daily discharge retrieval for American River nr Nile (gauge ~12488500) for NSE evaluation
Spin-up (accelerated decomposition + final) to equilibrate soil moisture and snowpack before evaluation period
assumptions: GSWP3 (or user-provided) forcing for 1980-2018 is representative at the site; first 2-3 years treated as model spin-up and excluded from NSE
NSE, if reported, will be computed on area-scaled total runoff vs observed daily Q as an approximation and clearly labeled as un-routed; a routed MOSART run is required for defensible NSE
Column soil textures assigned from SSURGO/gridded soil data along the elevation transect; refine with local surveys if available
Daily history output (nhtfrq set to daily averaging) is used to match the daily observation cadence
Vegetation/PFT taken from default surface dataset (montane conifer/shrub mix typical of the eastern Cascades)
